action: Customers of JPMorgan, Mastercard and Visa programs: expect phishing that uses your name or email, and do not act on unsolicited messages.
date_note: Date of the companies' statements: ABC13 (read 2026-11-19) says JPMorganChase made its statement Thursday morning (19 November); the date of the attack itself is not stated.
exec: Vendor breach exposed marketing data at major payment and banking brands; phishing risk for customers.
plain: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say outside vendors were hacked. JPMorgan and Mastercard say some customer email addresses may be exposed; they say card payment data was not.
summary: JPMorganChase said third-party providers were hit and attackers accessed marketing data that may include some customer names and email addresses. Mastercard cited a limited number of cardholder emails; Visa tied it to an Asia Pacific provider. n0n claimed it, per SOCRadar, unverified. Analytics Insight, relaying Reuters, cites a Reuters review of the leaked information that found more than 16,000 customer email addresses.
title: Visa, JPMorgan and Mastercard say third-party providers were hit; n0n gang claims it, per SOCRadar

validation.note: Second review: Cybernews (source 1) returns HTTP 403, so the claim that n0n listed Visa and JPMorgan by name is unverified. Yahoo (published 2026-11-19) says only that n0n claimed credit for the attacks, per SOCRadar. ABC13 does not mention

review.note: Compared with Yahoo, ABC13, Analytics Insight: statements, Mastercard, Visa APAC, n0n per SOCRadar match; 16,000 emails figure now says Reuters review of leaked information (article does not say JPMorgan data)
